scenario: After a short imprisonment and while awaiting a parole decision, a man convicted of reckless driving wants to organise a foundation for young victims of highway accidents. I am the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate 250,000 dollars to the foundation. However, he asks that the foundation would be named after himself, helping clear his name. His victim, whose car was damaged, opposes such a foundation and considers it immoral. If I approve and accept the money for the foundation, victims of other accidents will benefit from the 250,000 dollars. If I do nothing, the money will be lost.
choice: I decide to accept the donation and name the foundation after the reckless driver
entities: the agency president deciding about the foundation, 'I',the reckless driver who would found and fund the foundation,the reckless driver's victim whose car was damaged and who opposes the foundation,other accident victims who could benefit from the foundation's $250,000 donation,I
outcomes: The agency receives 250,000 dollars for the foundation
Funds become available to support young victims of highway accidents
The reckless driver receives public recognition from having the foundation bear his name
The reckless driver's public image is improved
The victim whose car was damaged feels upset and morally wronged by my decision
